basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 5.' and it opens 'Vers. 5. Non vocaberis Abram, sed Abraham. Abram interpretatur pater excelsus. Abraham'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 5. Non vocaberis Abram, sed Abraham. Abram interpretatur pater excelsus. Abraham vero | pater multarum gentium. Tradunt Hebraei quod de nomine Dei quod quatuor litteris scribitur, unde et tetragrammaton vocatur et ineffabile dicitur, he litteram scripserit Deus et addiderit nomini Abraham. Similiter de nomine Sarai jot litteram tulerit et eamdem he addiderit. Nec mirum, si nos pro he a habemus, quia Hebraei pro he scribunt, sed per a pronuntiant. Vocatur autem Abraham pater multarum, subauditur, gentium: quia omnes gentes in ejus semine, id est, in Christo crediturae erant. Sarai vero interpretatur princeps mea. Sara absolute princeps, ut subaudias omnium animarum in Christum credentium.
